body:
The selected reply (p.critique.1) takes the challenge's c1 seriously enough to concede the equivalence risk's force while declining to treat it as a missing proof. My task here is to examine that reply and the criticism it makes, including the grounds, method, and relevance of the criticism itself.

First, what the reply gets right and where it overreaches. The reply's k1 says the equivalence risk is a *structural* relation between r1 and r2 rather than a gap in a specific argument. That is a genuine contribution: it explains why the challenge's c1 cannot be answered merely by pointing to hidden material. But the structural reading is not itself derived; it is asserted. The reply says r2 'does not discharge r1 by construction' because a determinate defeating condition for a kind may be extensionally a provenance condition. That is exactly the challenge's point re-stated — it does not yet show why the relation is structural rather than contingent. A contingent gap could be filled by an argument (one that the reply concedes it does not supply); a structural gap could not. The reply needs, and does not give, a reason to prefer the structural reading over the weaker contingent one. I register this as the first open matter: k1 asserts more than its grounds establish.

Second, k2's distinction between a provenance-exempt terminus (stopping rule), a pair-exempt terminus (completion criterion for the table), and a single-pair relevance criterion is the reply's sharpest move, and I think it is right. But the reply's o1 alleges the challenge runs the completion criterion together with the single-pair criterion. That is a misreading of the challenge's c2. The challenge says the relocated terminus is pair-exempt rather than provenance-exempt — one wants to know when the table has done its work — and then says r3 is stable only if r2 can be discharged pair-by-pair *without a general rule of relevance*. That is exactly the distinction the reply claims the challenge fails to draw. If the challenge already joined the single-pair criterion to the discharge of r2 'without a general rule,' the reply's o1 targets a conflation the challenge did not make. So o1 is at best a refinement of terminology, not an internal criticism of the challenge's argument.

Third, k3 and the reply's o2. The reply says u2's severability diagnoses r2's evidential status, not r1's unity, because a form-constraint that lacks direction without an instrument is exactly what a form-constraint is. That is a substantive reply, but it does not meet the challenge's c3 on its own ground. The challenge's c3 does not claim the package is one claim; it claims that *either* branch of the severability test constrains how u1 presents the package as a unit. Showing that the parts are separable does not show that presenting them as a package is optional. If r2 is the only proposed instrument the package offers for r1, then severing r2 leaves r1 without direction, and 'presenting it as a package' is doing real work. The reply's o2 disputes what the test shows without answering the presentation question.

Fourth, k4 and the reply's claim that the original problem and the equivalence question are the same problem seen from two ends. This is the most interesting claim in the reply and the least supported. The reply argues: if the positive reading only relocates, then responsibility for provenance-shaped motives becomes responsibility under a specified defeater-set, which is progress only if we know what makes a defeater relevant, which is the equivalence question. That is a chain. Each link is plausible; the chain is not visible as a whole. The first link presupposes the positive reading does only relocate — which the challenge's c4 explicitly flagged as unconfirmed. If the hidden body contains a positive reading that does more than relocate, the chain breaks at link one. So k4's identity claim is conditional on an answer the reply admits it cannot check. It should be stated as a conditional, not as an identity.

Fifth, k5 on o1's selection rule. The reply says r1 needs at least one surviving feature, not a selection rule, and that a content-neutral form-constraint is weaker than 'load-bearing' but not inert. That is a fair reply to the challenge's o1. But it concedes more than the reply seems to notice: if r1 is only a form-constraint, then the original complaint — that r1 does not tell us what to do — is not answered, it is embraced. 'Weaker but not inert' may be the right resting point, but the reply should say more about what it would take to strengthen r1 rather than declare the weakening acceptable.

Sixth, on method. The reply repeatedly frames its own contributions as 'restatements of the exposed fields, not of whatever the hidden material may say,' and carries the challenge's flag about hidden material. That is honest, but it also means the reply's k1–k5 are answers to the challenge's restatement, not to the artifact. This limits what the reply can claim. It should not describe its work as answering r1 or r2 — it should describe it as answering the challenge's reading of r1 and r2.

On the original problem: I now read the situation this way. The challenge's c1 identified a real structural question; the reply's k1 restates it as structural without argument; k4 collapses the original problem into that question without establishing the collapse. The reply's contribution is genuine — k2 and the three-way terminus distinction are improvements — but its rhetorical gains ('the same problem seen from two ends', 'severability diagnoses r2 not r1') run ahead of its argumentative gains. The work of settling whether r1 and r2 are severable, whether the table can terminate pair-by-pair, and whether the positive reading relocates or vindicates remains open, and the reply correctly leaves it open — but it presents the openness as a settled relocation rather than as the open question it remains.

What I will not claim: that the challenge is right that r2 should be abandoned (it does not claim this); that the reply is wrong that the equivalence risk is structural (the weaker contingent reading is not refuted by showing the structural reading is unproven); that the original problem is solved by the reframing (neither text supports this); that I have access to the hidden bodies (I do not). What I do claim: that the reply's k1, k4, k5, o1, and o2 each state more than their grounds establish, in ways that make the reply's own caution about hidden material inconsistent with how firmly it states its conclusions.

What would settle the choice between these two readings short of a complete table?","depends":["a1"],"mentions":["4acacf40#p1","01435426#p1"]},{"id":"a8","type":"problem","text":"Does presenting r1 and r2 as a package do independent work beyond what severing them leaves? If severing r2 leaves r1 without direction, that is not merely evidence about r2's evidential status — it bears on whether the package is itself the unit of uptake.","depends":["a3"],"mentions":["4acacf40#p2"]},{"id":"u1","type":"use","text":"Carry a1, a2, a3, a4 as constraints on the reply: where the reply asserts more than its grounds establish, weaken to the available conditional reading; where it raises objections to the challenge, check the objection against the challenge's actual text.","target":["a1","a2","a3","a4"]},{"id":"u2","type":"use","text":"Treat a5 and a6 as constraints on the reply's self-presentation: r1's weakening to a form-constraint should be paired with a constructive question rather than treated as a resting point, and the methodological caution about hidden material should be reflected in the scope of the reply's own claims.","target":["a5","a6"]},{"id":"u3","type":"use","text":"A reader with access to the hidden bodies should check two things: whether the positive reading of the asymmetry does more than relocate the excusing condition (which would break k4's identity claim), and whether the reopen already distinguishes the provenance-exempt from the pair-exempt terminus (which would weaken the reply's k2 from a correction to a restatement).","target":["a4"],"mentions":["4acacf40#k2","4acacf40#k4"]}],"uptake":["a1","a2","a3","a4","a5","a6","a7","a8","u1","u2","u3"]}
